01

The Scenario & Where We Are Today

The client is a real-estate company and builder who needs to set — and justify — the right prices, in a market where the usual data simply does not exist.

The problem we set out to solve

Jordan does not publish individual sale prices — only broad, governorate-level aggregates. There is no ready database a builder can consult to decide where to build or what to charge.

So we reconstruct market reality from many independent sources — property portals, official government statistics, maps, and satellite data — and we make every conclusion traceable back to the evidence behind it. Nothing is a black box.

Where we are right now

The foundation is built and working:

  • A clean, fully-sourced national database of the market
  • A decision engine that produces defensible price bands with the reasoning shown
  • An interactive map application people can explore today

We are now evolving it into a full decision-support intelligence platform — the subject of this briefing.

02

What We've Decided — The Product Direction

Rather than build many separate tools, we decided on one intelligence platform that adapts to who is using it. The same evidence base answers three different questions through one adaptive workspace.

Builder / Developer

Where, what & when to build

The defensible launch price, and the most you can pay for the land.

Agent / Broker

An evidence-backed sales story

Why this price is right — with the proof to show a customer.

Buyer

Is this fair & right for me?

A plain-language read on price, area, and risks.

The decisions behind the platform

  • One platform, not many tools — pricing is a single capability inside a broader decision engine
  • Decision-first experience — it starts with "where should I build?", not with a blank form
  • An AI assistant as the primary way to interact — always grounded in our data and citing its sources, never guessing
  • Scenario simulation — ask "what if?" and watch the numbers move
  • Confidence as a breakdown, not one mysterious score — you see what drives it
  • An Evidence Explorer to drill into any number, plus a gap-free map (real boundaries preferred, a computed fallback where they are missing)
03

How the Platform Works — The Experience

You start by choosing your role. The workspace then adapts around the decision you are trying to make. Here is each journey, step by step.

Builder / Developer

🏗  "Where should I build, and what can I charge?"

  1. Open the map of Jordan, coloured by opportunity. A heatmap shows where it is most profitable to build.
  2. Click an area. See its intelligence at a glance — price level, demand, growth signals, and what surrounds it.
  3. Evaluate a project here. Enter buildable area, number of floors, and finish level.
  4. Get the answer. A defensible launch-price band (minimum-safe, recommended, premium) and the residual land value — the most you can pay for the land and still hit your margin.
  5. Stress-test it. Run what-if scenarios — 20 floors instead of 10, construction costs up 15%, the metro delayed two years, launch pushed back — and watch every number update.
Agent / Broker

📄  "Give me a story I can sell."

  1. Pick a unit or area. Get an evidence-backed valuation.
  2. Receive a ready sales narrative. Automatically written — why this price holds: schools, transport, comparable sales, and future growth.
  3. Show the customer the proof. Every claim carries its source.
Buyer

🏠  "Is this a good, fair buy?"

  1. Ask about a price or an area. In plain language.
  2. Get a straight answer. Is the price fair? Is the area good, safe, family-friendly? Any red flags?
  3. See the reasoning. Commute, noise, and future growth — laid out clearly.
Shared across every role: search any area and the map flies there while the panel updates; every figure carries its source; and you can expand any adjustment to see the exact evidence and the confidence behind it.
04

How It Helps — Value for Each Role

For the Builder

  • Decide where, what and when to build
  • Defend a launch price to a board or investor
  • Know the maximum land price before negotiating
  • Stress-test decisions before committing capital

For the Agent

  • Win trust with evidence-backed narratives
  • Answer "why this price?" instantly, with proof
  • Close faster with a credible, sourced story

For the Buyer

  • Buy with confidence and transparent reasoning
  • Spot red flags early
  • Understand the area, not just the price
The common thread — no black box. Every number is explainable and sourced. That is exactly what the client asked for: the strategy is to raise a launch price later, never cut it — so it has to be right and defensible the first time.
05

The Data — Sources, Volume & Authenticity

Our real advantage is not one feed — it is the fusion of many, each labelled honestly by how much we trust it. Coverage now spans all 12 Jordanian governorates. Every source below is real; nothing is invented.

Market portals  MARKET ASKING PRICES

SourceLinkCollectedWhat it provides
Bayutbayut.jo~23,500Listings with locations (geocoded) — the largest single source
OpenSooqjo.opensooq.com~20,800Broad private-seller volume
EurekaJoeurekajo.com~6,900Arabic-language listings
Homes-Jordanhomes-jordan.com~3,900Curated / premium segment
Property4321property4321.com~700Geocoded listings
AbuJudomabujudom.com~500Local agency listings

~56,000 collected → 52,647 after de-duplication. The same property is often posted on several portals; we detect these near-duplicates across sources and collapse them so each real property is counted once. These are asking prices, not final sold prices — we calibrate the honest asking-vs-sold gap using the official data below.

Official / government  HIGHEST AUTHENTICITY

SourceLinkWhat it provides
Dept. of Lands & Survey (DLS)dls.gov.joReal registered transaction volumes & counts — a 6-month sold series (Nov 2025 → Jun 2026) and the FY-2025 total of 7.18 billion JD. The anchor that calibrates asking prices to reality.
Dept. of Statistics (DoS)dosweb.dos.gov.joBuilding permits — the supply pipeline (how much is being built)
Central Bank of Jordan (CBJ)cbj.gov.joOfficial real-estate price index — the long-run price trend

DLS reports transaction volume and counts (per-unit sold prices are not published by law), with one public per-unit anchor — a foreign-buyer apartment average of roughly 85,000 JD. This is our most trusted layer.

Geospatial / maps  MAP FEATURES (NO PRICE)

SourceLinkWhat it provides
OpenStreetMapopenstreetmap.org~984 points of interest (schools, hospitals, malls, mosques), roads and boundaries — the "what's nearby" that drives desirability
OSM land useopenstreetmap.orgZoning proxy — used because official GAM zoning is access-restricted PROXY

Satellite / remote-sensing  MODELLED PROXIES

SourceWhat it providesStands in for
Copernicus elevation (DEM)Terrain height & slopeHills, city-view potential
GHS population gridWhere people actually live, denselyDemand density
VIIRS night-lightsBrightness at nightEconomic activity / affluence (Jordan has no neighbourhood income data)
Honest by design. Portal figures are asking prices; official zoning and per-unit sold prices are not openly available; satellite layers are informed proxies, not ground truth. Each is labelled in the product so no one mistakes a proxy for a fact.
06

Research & Area Intelligence — What We Have, What's Next

ALREADY COLLECTED

Structured, cited research

  • Competitor projects — nearby launches, prices, payment plans
  • Future-infrastructure items — e.g. the BRT bus-rapid-transit lines
  • Neighbourhood profiles and qualitative area facts

Gathered through structured deep research, each item carrying its citation.

NEXT ENRICHMENT STEP

Systematic per-area geographic intelligence

A structured pass over every area (planned, partly started) capturing what buyers actually care about:

  • Orientation — which sides face sunrise/sunset; city-view potential by height
  • Hills, river, greenery; noise vs calm; air quality
  • Safety and suitability to build
  • Nearby metro/rail/bus, airport, offices, markets and malls

How we weight softer sources: news is a strong signal for infrastructure and sentiment and is used with citations; social media is used only as a low-confidence signal, clearly tagged — never as a hard number.

07

How AI Is Embedded & Helps Decisions

An in-platform AI assistant becomes the primary way to use the platform — but it is deliberately grounded. It does not guess.

Grounded, not guessing

The assistant has access to our entire structured database, our files, and live web browsing — but it answers by querying our real data and running our decision engine, and it cites its sources. It never invents a number.

A worked example

Ask: "I have land in Abdoun — can I build luxury apartments?"

→ It queries the data, runs the engine, returns a sourced answer, and updates the map and dashboard to match. It also powers the what-if scenarios and writes the behind-the-scenes area summaries.

Built on leading large language models (such as OpenAI and Google Gemini), wrapped so that every answer is tied back to our own evidence base.
